summary: Practiced only once in training camp before a calf injury sidelined him; has gone from competing for a starting spot to fighting to make the 53-man roster ahead of the Aug. 30 cutdown deadline. Kyle Shanahan said the 49ers may place him on IR rather than cut him outright.

2026 2nd-round rookie (33rd overall) had 7 catches for 63 yards in the first half alone of his preseason debut vs. Tennessee, drawing praise from Brock Purdy and George Kittle. With Ricky Pearsall out for the season and Christian Kirk injury-limited, Stribling has a real path to early snaps as a rookie with no prior-season stat line to project from.
source: NBC Sports Bay Area/SF Chronicle/Niners Nation

summary: Remains Cleveland's most polished receiver and likely first perimeter option to open the season, but the Browns doubled up at WR in the draft (KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston); by season's end analysts project Boston as WR1 and Concepcion as WR2, with Jeudy's target share expected to erode as the rookies take over.

2026 draft pick who performed as advertised at rookie minicamp alongside fellow rookie KC Concepcion; his size (6'4", 212 lbs) complements Concepcion's speed in HC Todd Monken's offense. Analysts project him to be Cleveland's WR1 by season's end, ahead of incumbent Jerry Jeudy.

Listed as Seattle's clear WR2 behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba on the most current depth chart (Aug. 25), ahead of new signing Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton (currently injured) — retains a strong role despite the offseason additions to the room.

Signed with Seattle in the offseason but sits behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Rashid Shaheed (and, when healthy, Tory Horton) on the current depth chart — a clear WR3/4 role rather than the WR1 usage his career track record with the Rams reflects.

Fully recovered from the cracked tibia that ended his 2025 rookie season, but a new, undisclosed injury has sidelined him during 2026 preseason camp — he missed Seattle's Aug. 15 preseason opener and HC Mike Macdonald says he'll be out "for a period of time."

For the first time in his career, Tucker enters camp as the Raiders' clear top receiving option after leading the team in receiving yards (696) and a career-high 5 TDs in 2025. Getting heavy first-team reps with both Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza, plus a return-game role.

4th-round 2026 rookie named a starting wide receiver on the Titans' first unofficial depth chart under new OC Brian Daboll, ahead of veteran depth — a real Week 1 role with no NFL stat history to project from.

Expected to see the field in Tennessee's opener and counted on for a rotational role in the reshaped Daboll offense, behind the team's bigger free-agent/rookie additions (Wan'Dale Robinson, Carnell Tate, Calvin Ridley).

Rookie has moved well ahead of Roman Wilson on Pittsburgh's depth chart during camp, logging significantly more outside-WR snaps as the top backup to Michael Pittman Jr. — a reversal of the team's initial (pre-camp) depth chart.
Started camp as Pittsburgh's slot starter but rookie Germie Bernard has since passed him on the depth chart; Wilson has also struggled beating press coverage as an outside receiver during camp.

Still an unsigned free agent as of late August; per ESPN, the Chargers are not planning to add another veteran WR and feel good about rookie Brenen Thompson's camp performance. Allen's only realistic path back to the Chargers is an injury elsewhere on the roster — he should not be projected as rostered anywhere for 2026 barring news.
Rookie's strong camp performance is a direct reason the Chargers have decided not to pursue a Keenan Allen reunion, per ESPN — earning real WR-room trust as a rookie with no NFL stat history.
Signed a new three-year contract, locking him in through at least 2029 and cementing his role as a core piece of Carolina's receiving corps ahead of Xavier Legette on the current depth chart.

2024 1st-round pick suffered a stinger in camp practice (avoided a concussion, shouldn't miss extended time), and separately has fallen behind Jalen Coker on the depth chart after Coker's new extension — real uncertainty around his role for a former first-rounder.
2026 3rd-round rookie (Tennessee) is out for the entire 2026 season after tearing his LCL in a practice. No 2026 projection should be used for him at all.

Signed a one-year deal (up to $6.5M) with Philadelphia after Kansas City; became an immediate upgrade at the No. 3 WR spot once A.J. Brown was traded to New England, working outside opposite DeVonta Smith on the post-trade depth chart.

2nd-year UDFA (9 catches, 92 yards as a rookie) is drawing real praise from Jalen Hurts in his second training camp, competing for a role behind DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon — both currently dealing with hamstring injuries, which opens a path to more camp reps.
Entering his third season, Walker is seen as the favorite for Baltimore's WR3 role over rookies Ja'Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt, having made the most of his opportunities so far in camp.

Listed as Baltimore's starting WR2 on the team's unofficial depth chart behind only Zay Flowers, and new OC Declan Doyle is using him in the slot significantly more than in prior seasons — an expanded role beyond his 2025 usage.

2026 3rd-round rookie (Clemson, No. 71 overall) is currently projected as Washington's No. 4 WR behind Terry McLaurin, newly-signed Stefon Diggs, and Luke McCaffrey — the Diggs signing pushed his rookie-year path down a notch before camp even started.
Signed as a free agent this offseason; currently projects as the Giants' No. 4 WR behind Malik Nabers, Darius Slayton, and rookie Malachi Fields in a crowded receiver room.
Positioned as the Giants' clear No. 2 receiving option behind Malik Nabers on the current depth chart, ahead of the team's other offseason additions at the position.
The Giants' significant draft investment in Fields suggests he'll be the team's No. 3 receiving option as a rookie, in a crowded room that also added Darnell Mooney and Isaiah Hodgins in free agency.

Re-signed with the Giants but is buried in one of the deepest WR rooms in the league (Nabers, Slayton, Fields, Mooney all ahead of him) — described as possibly his final opportunity to stick with the team.
Suffered a torn Achilles that reportedly helped spur the Giants' trio of veteran WR free-agent signings this offseason. Braxton Berrios is now expected to handle the primary return role in his place.

3rd-round 2026 rookie was named a starting WR on Miami's first unofficial preseason depth chart and has separated himself as QB Malik Willis's most reliable target in camp, ahead of veterans Jalen Tolbert and Malik Washington.
Coming off a 46-catch, 317-yard 2025, Washington now sits behind rookie Caleb Douglas on Miami's post-Tyreek-Hill/Jaylen-Waddle-overhaul WR depth chart despite having more NFL experience.

3rd-round 2026 rookie tore his ACL in November 2025 (pre-draft), did not practice all spring, and is expected to open camp on the PUP list — a designation that could carry into the regular season, per team reporting.

Former UDFA (26 catches, 193 yards in 2025) has elevated his standing after strong OTA/minicamp/camp performances and is now viewed as the Jets' top receiver reserve behind starters Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell, plus a return-game role.

2026 3rd-round pick, primarily valued for a return-specialist role behind veteran additions Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus on Atlanta's receiver depth chart — limited near-term receiving upside as a rookie.
Cut by the Falcons as part of an offseason receiver-room overhaul (Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus signed, Zachariah Branch drafted). No longer on Atlanta's roster.
Signed with Atlanta in free agency after a 39-catch, 313-yard 2025 with the Bears; slots into a veteran depth role behind Drake London and Jahan Dotson in a retooled Falcons receiver room.

Second-year receiver suffered a season-ending torn ACL in training camp after being expected to start alongside Nico Collins. The Texans responded by signing veterans Zay Jones and Sterling Shepard and trading for Kayshon Boutte. No 2026 projection should use his 2025 role.

After not making the roster out of camp the prior year, Flournoy worked his way back and had a breakout second-year season; now holds Dallas's No. 3 WR role behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, ahead of newcomer Marquez Valdes-Scantling and rookie Jordan Hudson.

Traded from Denver to New Orleans; has the early edge at WR3 on the Saints' unofficial depth chart entering the preseason, a clean-slate opportunity in a much more open receiver room than the one he left behind.

2026 3rd-round rookie (Georgia State) has the physical tools to eventually challenge for Tampa Bay's starting X role but will likely spend his rookie camp getting up to speed and contributing on special teams first.

Second-year receiver has been a big-play threat through the first week of camp, building on a rookie season with 5 TDs on 44 targets despite a 5'10", 165-lb frame — trending toward an expanded role in Tampa Bay's post-Mike-Evans receiver room.
Valued primarily as Tampa Bay's best return specialist rather than as a receiving weapon — limited near-term fantasy relevance beyond special teams.

His snap share fell sharply in 2025 (26% of offensive snaps, career lows in targets/catches/yards), and New England then traded for A.J. Brown and signed Romeo Doubs this offseason, pushing him further down the depth chart into a rotational role.

3rd-round 2026 rookie (LSU) is listed third-string on Chicago's first unofficial August depth chart, but has impressed coaches and teammates enough at minicamp that the team is expected to find him a meaningful role in Ben Johnson's offense.
Currently leading the competition for Denver's WR3 role over rookie Pat Bryant and Troy Franklin, per the most recent preseason lineup order, behind top duo Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton.

Rookie is in a three-way camp battle with Marvin Mims Jr. and Troy Franklin for Denver's WR3 role behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton; currently behind Mims in the pecking order per the latest preseason lineup.

Now clearly set as part of Kansas City's starting WR trio alongside Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy, per RotoWire's 2026 depth chart — a significant role upgrade after bouncing through New England and Chiefs' practice squad waiver claims.

2025 1st-round pick dealt with a toe injury during camp but has returned to practice and remains one of Green Bay's three starting receivers alongside Christian Watson and Jayden Reed; could be with the team through 2029 if the fifth-year option is exercised.
